Our love language? Spending money at local businesses ☕💐🧁 

Shop small this Small Business Saturday!

Justice from Byronandco is preparing for Black Friday, one to-do list at a time. 🐾

First up: what to restock. She asked JAX in Xero what sold the most last month. The answer? Dog treats in a can.

With stock covered, she ran a 72-hour early access sale this year, up from 24 last year. (Her mum, her bookkeeper and BAS agent, approves.)

Ask JAX what's selling. Then get back to the packing. ✅

Her home kitchen sparked a Singaporean food business 🍜

Megan Tan started yummsinga alongside her full-time job, with a simple idea: help people enjoy authentic Singaporean cuisine.

Being new to the market, she needed to know what was working. With Xero, she can compare sales from in-person events with online, and put her effort where it counts.

'It gives me the confidence for the business.' 💙

JAX handles the follow-ups, so the texts with my accountant can be about the good stuff 💙
Tag the accountant this one’s for.

For more ways to feel confident with your business admin, read the On Hand Guide. Link in bio.

Almost 5,000 workshop guests later, the family story keeps growing 🌿

Charly and Yuvey grew up helping their parents sell terrariums in Venezuela. In 2019, they brought that legacy to New York as Terrart, building it out with ecommerce, wholesale and hands-on workshops.

With Xero showing their numbers in real time, admin dropped from 8–10 hours a week to 3–4. So when a decision can’t wait, the answer’s already there.

“Our mom and dad, they’re very, very proud.” 🪴❤️

PART 1 |  Biggest sale of the year… but have we ordered enough stock? 👀

For innerchildshop, Black Friday Cyber Monday is uncharted territory. With their first-ever BFCM sale on the horizon, the excitement is building, but so is the big question: have they ordered enough stock to keep up with demand?

The countdown is on, the stock is ordered, and now it's all about seeing what happens as they prepare for the sale goes live.

Stay tuned for Part 2....

Elon Musk’s US$9 billion brain-implant startup Neuralink has released footage of a paralysed clinical trial participant playing Grand Theft Auto VI with nothing but his mind.

Founded in 2016, the company has trials running in the US, Canada, the UK and the UAE, and had 26 patients enrolled in its main study. Its device is still investigational and has not been approved by the FDA.

Closer to home, Melbourne-founded rival Synchron has implanted its own device in patients in Australia and the US.

Black Friday discounts are leaving some shoppers with purchases they wish they’d never made, according to new research by Finder.
Finder’s Shopping Report 2026 reveals 16% of Australians have bought something in a Black Friday sale that they later regretted or never used. That’s 3.5 million people.

Did you snap up any bargains in the Black Friday sales?

#blackfriday #christmasshopping #sales #shopping

Finder’s 2026 Shopping Report revealed Australians set to spend $5.1 billion on Black Friday.

Shoppers are expected to spend $236 each on average on Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

#blackfriday #christmasshopping #sales #shopping

This striking pavilion style residence in Orford is surrounded by native bushland, with the architecture welcoming the outside in and the surrounding bushland becoming part of everyday life 😍 The pavilion style residence offers a wonderful sense of privacy, space and connection to nature, with soft ocean glimpses appearing through the trees.
 
💰 Price guide: $3,795,000 - $3,895,000

‘Sweetwater Estate’ offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity in the heart of the Hunter Valley 😮 The property is set across approximately 48 hectares of magnificent countryside and looks like something straight out of the European countryside.
 
Think soaring vaulted ceilings, sweeping staircases, vine-clad Juliet balconies and arched doorways to name just a few features of this grand estate 😍

A 165-year-old church is on the market, offering not just a slice of Adelaide Hills history but its own graveyard 👀⁠
⁠
The foundation stone of the Bull Creek Primitive Methodist Church was laid by preacher Thirza Middlebrook on October 30, 1860. The property was last purchased around 2000, with the current owner transforming it into a cosy one-bedroom home that could be used as an Airbnb by investors or for downsizers.⁠
⁠
Tap the 🔗 in our bio to read the story. ⁠

Timeless architecture and extraordinary natural beauty come together in this incredible landmark estate in the heart of the Byron hinterland 😍⁠

⁠
A rare opportunity to enjoy the privacy and tranquillity of such a large estate, while still being close to Byron Bay
